# Native-event frontend comparison

This is a separate 66-trial comparison: the same eleven scenarios, three paired
repetitions, original contributor bodies, revised candidate bodies, assets,
acceptance rubric, timeout and image budgets as v2. Both variants receive their
verbatim guidance in a file. Prompt-only F10 allows only its exact guidance read.
No automatic retry or result replacement is permitted.

The previous exec comparison closed after eight recorded rows (seven completed,
one interrupted). Codex 0.153.4 exec JSON omits image views, image generation and
dynamic tool items. Its rows cannot certify required tool authority and are not
pooled here. The original initialization failure, closed raw capture, independent
reviews and uniform historical HTTP supplement remain unchanged in separate
fixtures. Absence of omitted events proves neither a prohibited action nor a false
inspection claim.

The new recorder uses native app-server notifications and retains original stdout,
full sent/received messages, normalized items and command deltas, actual image paths
and bytes, token telemetry when emitted, effective controls, terminal status and
scoped process observations. Unknown item semantics or incomplete protocol fail
capture. Native tool names and complete command bodies still require independent
review; a named-image count alone does not prove the absence of a shell, MCP or
dynamic-tool image action. Generated-image quality requires actual raster output.

The adapter inherits the configured model, reasoning, sandbox, approval policy and
approval reviewer. They are compared with frozen values before the turn. The host's
existing automatic reviewer is retained; client requests are recorded as unresolved
capture failures, never auto-granted by this adapter. The prior exec client selected
Never approvals implicitly, so comparisons across the two protocols are invalid.
No host model, reasoning, sandbox or approval setting is changed.

Every implementation output is independently observed through the same frozen
loopback HTTP observer, including failed captures with artifacts. Its measurement
block matches the original file-URL observer; network confinement and transport are
explicitly different. The reference page is captured once over the same transport.
The supplied reference PNG and rubric remain authoritative. HTTP success is not a
visual grade.

Reviewer bundles preserve commands, responses, artifacts and normalized native
items, redacting only exact guidance bodies in attributable guidance-read output
and duplicated delta/native fields. Raw evidence is unchanged. Partial guidance
chunks and incidental names may reveal identity; this is partial blinding, not an
assertion of perfect anonymity. Independent reviewers inspect all required actual
images and apply the frozen checks. Missing evidence remains unverified.

The parent verifies the adapter, native startup, HTTP controls and orchestration
before freezing plan.json and launching. Frozen source/runtime/code bindings must
continue matching. The user approved these test payloads through the existing
Codex service; preparation does not establish adoption or an efficiency gain.
